English: Grant Equal Rights to the White Ruthenians

While far from our height many centuries ago, our recent conquest of White Ruthenia puts our nation in a peculiar position. Even if there were always Slavs in our nation after our independence, now, with the inclusion of our old territories, the White Ruthenians became a sizeable portion of our population, with our people becoming a minority in our own nation. Now, our ministers suggest that the best course of action would be to, instead of letting our peoples fight against each other within our own borders, we should integrate the people of White Ruthenia in our nation, granting them equal rights to Lithuanians and finding unity in our shared history under foreign rule.

With our victory in the Baltic, our new allies in the East soon will have to choose how their new nation will be governed. As the guarantors of their independence, we naturally hold a great deal of influence with them, being offered to send representatives to the upcoming meeting in Riga. We should decide what will be our agenda in Riga and in which direction we will sway their decision into.

With the consolidation of Baltic administration and our underhand deal with Berlin struck, we are starting to take steps to make sure Russia can't curtail Baltic autonomy. Our people got in contact with Latvian and Estonian leaders, to talk about the possibility of Baltic independence, and for the nation to stay united as a state of Germans, Latvians and Estonians. Not only did we manage to strike a deal with their leadership, but they also offered to get in contact with some Latvians and Estonians in Dinaburg and Pechory to have them rise up and join the Baltic struggle for independence. Now, with everything ready, all that is left is to cast the die and depose our Russian overlords.

§RGain 12.5 infamy§! When the Baltic was first conquered from Sweden, Peter the Great of Russia handed the ruling of the Baltic to his, very corrupt, right-hand man and governor of Ingria. While he fell from the position even before the governorates were properly established, with our position in the Baltic and independence from Russia secured, the ambitions of our state grew, and Ingria became subject to the interest of war hawks and jingoists alike. With our independence, the Russian government has formally declared the transfer of the Imperial Capital from Saint Petersburg to Moscow, undoing Peter the Great's work, with some arguing that now would be the perfect time to claim Ingria. If we were to seize Ingria and St. Petersburg, we would be pretty much expelling Russia from the Baltic Sea, forever tarnishing the legacy their tsars fought to build.

§RGain 2 infamy§! Despite being once a great state in Eastern Europe, after being partitioned time and time again, the Polish people were divided between Austria, Prussia and Russia. Now, with our significant influence in Polish lands, we could not only partially right this wrong, but also strengthen our Polish allies by pushing to unite Poland with Galicia-Lodomeria, while also taking the opportunity to solve some minor claims the Polish have on us. While the Polish people sure will appreciate the unification, the other powers won't be pleased to see us redrawing Eastern Europe in such a way.

§RGain 3 infamy§! While we were considered by many as a power in decline after the Napoleonic Wars and the loss of Norway, it has become clear that those years of humiliation are behind us. As our nation is once again respected on the world stage, it would only be natural that we start looking into old claims that we could use to solidify our newfound position and prestige. One of the bolder suggestions circulating within our government is that of the Estonian claim. Not only because we held it as a duchy for about a century, but also due to the importance of Estonia in regard to our history - with the legend about the origins of the Dannebog, our flag, in the Battle of Lindanise, during the Livonian Crusade.

With our recent defeats in the Baltic, we took a significant blow to our international status. The annexation of the Baltic in the Great Northern War under Peter the Great centuries ago elevated Russia into a true European power and, while the loss of the Baltic won't undermine our position as major player in European politics, we can't deny that it left a sour taste in our mouths. To remedy that, we could reassert our position in the Baltic Sea and claim that the Baltic states do not deserve independence and are still an integral part of our territory.

Ever since the end of the Byzantine Empire, the Greek people have never been unified into a single nation. While Attica and Peloponnese managed to be part of the new Greek nation, Greeks in the Aegean sea and Anatolia weren't so lucky, even if some of them recently managed to free themselves from Turkish overlordship. Now, with our control over Greece, the Greek people of the Aegean and Anatolia are skeptical of joining Greece, wary of our presence in the country. But, if we managed to increase our influence in these new states we could, in theory, make so their governments agree to join our Greek vassals, letting our puppet grow in strength.

§RGain 5 infamy§! The Balkans have always been a playground for foreign empires. As we strive to prove ourselves as a true great power in Europe, we seek a sphere of influence of our own, with the Balkans emerging as the most promising target. By expanding our influence in the region, we can strip the Austrians and Turks of territory while creating allies who will be forever indebted to us, securing our place as the Masters of the Adriatic.

§RGain 8 infamy§! The Balkans have always been a playground for foreign empires. Populated by South Slavic peoples, the region naturally falls within our sphere of influence, with many viewing us as brothers and liberators due to our role in freeing them from the Ottoman Empire. If we were to complete the liberation of the South Slavic people from the Ottoman and Austrian Empires, we could not only create a powerful ally but also gain access to a route that bypasses the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits, allowing us to establish a naval presence in the Mediterranean Sea.

§RGain 5 infamy§! The Balkans have always been a playground for foreign empires, including ourselves. We have long held an interest in the region, demonstrated by our control over Croatia and our rivalry with the Ottomans. While we have previously stated that we hold no interest in further expansion, the rise of nationalism has turned the Balkans into a powder keg waiting to explode. If we were to reassert our position, we might be able to organize the region in a way that quells the nationalist fires threatening to destabilize our empire in the future - even if it means angering Russia in the process.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Ever since our hegemony over Italy was established, our nation has only benefited — diplomatically, by having the entire peninsula as our ally, and economically, through French investors dominating Italy’s mines and factories. One such place is Sardinia. With its profitable mines and proximity to French Corsica, our investors have taken control of most of the economy on this otherwise isolated island. As a result, there has been growing outcry in Paris over the idea of annexing the island to secure its valuable resources. However, that is not to say the proposal has gone unopposed—many advisors argue that Sardinia has long been isolated from the rest of Italy and has a strong history of resisting outside influence. Still, our far-reaching economic presence may be a promising sign.
Now that we united our region, the time has come to reform New England!
With our control over Mongolia, we could expand Zheltorossiya and hand these lands over to the government in Harbin, that would, without a doubt, better be able to hold the Mongolian Steppes.
With our control over Xinjiang, we could expand Zheltorossiya and hand these lands over to the government in Harbin, that would, without a doubt, better be able to hold Dzungaria.

With our control over Xinjiang and Mongolia, we are almost reaching the final borders we planned for Zheltorossiya. What remains is to push through the Gansu province, so that our border follows the Yellow River. That would certainly make defense of the region easier, but contrary to the rest of Zheltorossiya, Gansu is densely populated, making it harder to control than the rest of Zheltorossiya.

As our first conquest in Central Asia, the land of the Kazakhs has been administered through the Governor-Generalship of the Steppes, primarily maintained by scattered Russian forts and pockets of Russian-dominated cities across the region. With the pacification of the area now complete, our next step is to encourage Russian settlement—taking advantage of the vast expanses of fertile land in northern and eastern Kazakhstan, even at the cost of disrupting nomadic routes and driving the Kazakhs our of their traditional grazing pastures, leaving them open to be transformed into Russian farms.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Despite having no desire to create a unified German nation, our victory against Prussia has granted us near-total hegemony over the former German Confederation—excluding only Prussia proper. This does not mean, however, that the winds of German nationalism have subsided, on the contrary, it remains the most serious threat to our hold over the Confederation. To secure our dominance, we could assert control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, enabling us to shape legislation that would entrench—and even expand—our hegemony over Germany without opposition.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states for us to consider, one of the most pressing ones would be the Rhineland. The lands along the Rhine have seen a significant boom in industrialization, which would greatly benefit our empire. Thus, we have put forth a proposal in the Federal Convention, to establish the Rhenish Industrial Commission which would, on paper,further boost industrialization in the Ruhr but, in reality, it would give us total control over the Rhenish affairs

§RGain 5 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states for us to consider, it recently came to our attention the matter of the duchy of Westphalia and the Hesse states. Westphalia has been under the control of a Habsburg noble ever since the end of the war against Prussia. But now, with our control over Frankfurt, we may change that. This time, one of our advisors has giving the idea of ordering the Duke of Westphalia to resign and partition his land between the states of Hesse, on the condition that they band together in the Union of Hesse-Westphalia and, of course, be loyal to us afterwards.

§RGain 8 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states to consider, one stands out: our loyal allies in Hanover. Having only recently gained independence from London, the Kingdom of Hanover has aligned with Austria from day one and supported the German Confederation in both Schleswig Wars. Perhaps it is time to reward this noble nation by expanding its territory—on the condition, of course, that it swears fealty to us.

§RGain 2.5 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states to consider, it is time we turn our attention to the Free and Hanseatic Cities of Bremen, Hamburg, and Lübeck. These cities aligned themselves with Prussia, giving us more than enough justification to simply incorporate them into Hanover and Mecklenburg. However, doing so would undoubtedly alienate many of the smaller states within the Confederation—most of which also sided with Prussia. Instead, we shall reform the Hanseatic League, uniting the three cities into a single state. This new entity will receive greater autonomy within the German Confederation, while still remaining subordinate to its executive authority—our emperor.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states to consider, the matter of the Saxon states now calls for our attention. The Kingdom of Saxony has long been our ally, with the Austrian Emperor having protected it from annexation by Prussia during the Congress of Vienna. It is now time to reward Saxony and ensure it remains within our sphere of influence—by uniting Thuringia with its kingdom. In doing so, we not only reward Saxony for its loyalty but also grant it jurisdiction over the Thuringian duchies—most of which sided with Prussia during our war against them.

§RGain 2.5 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states to consider, it is probably for the best that we get the question of Mecklenburg out of the way. The Duchy of Mecklenburg was an ally of Prussia, but there is no need to punish them. Instead, to guarantee their loyalty, we could unite them with the smaller Duchy of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, while also getting some concessions from them that would give us control over them.

§RGain 12.5 infamy§! Now that we hold control over the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, we can begin reorganizing Germany to secure our hegemony over the German Confederation. While there are many states to consider, an urgent matter is that of Brandenburg and Pomerania. Both states have been separated from Prussia and are currently under heavy oversight by both our Empire and the German Confederation. Needless to say, our control over the region is unstable—these lands were long held by the Hohenzollerns, and resistance to our rule is to be expected. Fortunately, one of our advisors has devised a plan: to forge a conspiracy suggesting that Brandenburg intends to return to Hohenzollern rule. This would provide us with the justification to declare martial law over both Brandenburg and Pomerania, allowing us to seize permanent control of the duchies.

The island of Heligoland is a small island off the coast of Germany, traditionally considered part of Schleswig or the Frisian Islands. With our control over the Frisian Islands, we maybe could try to buy Heligoland from the British. The island is small and over the years—instead of becoming a naval base—it evolved into a vacation spot and safe haven for German liberals, so they wouldn't mind handing them over to us—for a small price, of course.

After centuries being ruled from London, we are once again free from the English yoke! But now that we are finally free to pursue our own path, we can't deny that the English left a significant vacuum in the governance of our nation. 

That is why, if we are to enter the world stage and become a proper nation once again, we need to answer an important question: what is the source of legitimate power in our new nation?

As we grant a special place for the slavs in our nation, we have already granted rights to the Croats, but, with our centuries-long influence over the South Slavic peoples, it is only natural that we start striving to integrate all of the South Slavs into our nation, granting them a place in our Austro-Slavic union over the Danube.

After a total transformation of our nation into a Danubian Federation, the Romanians already have a place in our nation, due to them being the dominant population in Transylvania. But, with Romania under our influence, we could spend some political capital to integrate it into our nation, expanding the our nation until it reachs the Black Sea.

With our union with the Slavic people, one of the biggest slavic groups in our nation are the Polish. Naturally, ever since the partitions of Poland, we ruled over a significant Polish minority, keeping it even as Napoleon created the Duchy of Warsaw. Now, with the Polish becoming members of our Austro-Slavic nation, we have the change to protect the Polish from both Prussian and Russian threats, by integrating them into our nation once we manage to hold enough sway over them.

§RGain 10 infamy§! Despite enjoying German help to fight the Russians, we couldn't risk having the Germans taking the place of the Russians as our new overlords. Because of that, the revolution was born, with the Baltic people storming the Landtag and declaring the creation of $COUNTRY$. Despite that, we can't deny that Germany still holds lots of sway over our nation, bringing some question to the legitimacy of our regime. So, to quell any doubts about the sovereignty of $COUNTRY$, we shall prove ourselves to be a truly Baltic republic, by claiming Prussia, leaving it clear once and for all that we aren't mere subservient to Berlin. \n\n§RPulling yourself out of German protection is a dangerous game for the player, especially if you are a Radical Republic! Not only you will have no protector against Russia, but the European powers won't shy away from putting down a nation that openly defies the European order, no matter how puny it looks!§!

Despite being a Russian governate until recently, we managed to achieve a quite privileged position among Europena powers, despite maybe still not reaching the level of prestige and power of nations such as France and Britain. That, paired with our agressive expansion, left us wanting more. Now that we are free from outside influence, our nation grew more and more ambitious and, with the conquest of Prussia, we couldn't help but feel emboldened to persue such ambitions.
Officials from Japan are working with our government to oversee our own modernization. We hope to use their knowledge to pursue reforms in all aspects, from social to military.

The Mantetsu was established after the agressive takeover of most of the Russian Eastern China Railway, following the Japanese victory in the Russo-Japanese War. The company would grow rapidly, going beyond a simple railway company. Soon, the Mantetsu would expand its operations into coal mines, harbors, research centes and even hotels. Now, with our invasion of Manchuria, the Mantetsu became an essential part of our occupation of the region, not only becoming responsible for around 25% of our tax revenue, but also deeply penetrating every sphere of everyday life in Manchuria.

The company would grow rapidly, going beyond a simple railway company. Soon, the Mantetsu would expand its operations into coal mines, harbors, research centes and even hotels. Now, with our invasion of Manchuria, the Mantetsu became an essential part of our occupation of the region, not only becoming responsible for around 25% of our tax revenue, but also deeply penetrating every sphere of everyday life in Manchuria.

The company would grow rapidly, going beyond a simple railway company. Soon, the Mantetsu would expand its operations into coal mines, harbors, research centes and even hotels. Now, with our invasion of Manchuria, the Mantetsu became an essential part of our occupation of the region, not only becoming responsible for around 25% of our tax revenue, but also deeply penetrating every sphere of everyday life for Japanese settlers in Manchuria. \n\nNow, with the rise of Mangyo, most of Mantetsu investment has been absorved and repurposed into serving the developing Manchurian economy, Mantetsu's role has been devolved mainly into its railway lines, planning and research.

The Mantetsu engaged in a country-wide development project, with not only its Research Wing being a center piece of Japan's colonial program, but also devoloping the country's heavy industry and soybean agriculture, with land cultivation increasing in 70% in 20 years, not to mention the construction of schools, libraries and hospitals promoted by the Mantetsu.

Following the Japanese Invasion of Manchuria and the economic success of Mantetsu, the South Manchuria Railway Company helped the Kwantung Army develop a economic and industrial plan for the future of Manchuria, inviting Yoshisuke Aikawa, the founder of the Nissan zaibatsu who proposed the establishment of the Manchurian Industrial Development Company, also known as Mangyo, a joint venture owned 50% by Nissan and 50% by the Manshukoku government. \n\nDespite being rejected at first in favor of Kwantung plans, Aikawa soon would have its way, successfully pulling investment into Manchuria and integrating Mantetsu investments into the Mangyo, managing to surpass the Home Islands in certain sectors by the end of Mangyo's first five year plan.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Oman has been a target of Persian expansion ever since the days before the Islamic invasions, with Persia having last conquered Oman during the Asharid period, under Nader Shah in 1743, a mere century ago. 

In turn, after a prolonged civil war following the overthrow of Shah, Persia's most important port—Bandar Abbas—came under the control of the Imam of Muscat. A lease treaty confirming the port's status under Omani rule from 1794 has recently been revoked by our administration and—together with the invasion of Baluchistan and the western coast of Arabia—assured that our relations with Oman shifted in our favor. 

Now, while Oman has built quite an empire with their holdings in Africa, we hold the upper hand against them, being capable of not only seizing their Indian ports, but outright exile the Imam of Muscat to Zanzibar, giving us not only complete control over the Persian Gulf, but also seizing his lands in the Arabian Peninsula.

§RGain 4 infamy§! Seizing control over Western Arabia has solidified our position on the Persian Gulf, but stoping now wouble be neglecting the fact that our control over it remains unstable, with its waters being easily blockaded if any naval power were to take control over either side of the Hormuz Strait. With that, after we reintegrate Bandar Abbas and the Island of Hormu back into our rule after years of Omani rule, it would be only natural that, to trully secure the Persian Gulf, we invade the many emirates across the Hormuz Strait. \n\nAnnexing both sides of the Hormuz Strait would not only guarantee our control over the Persian Gulf, but also pacify the many emirs on the Arabian side of it, making sure that their in-fighting won't let western powers encroach in our backyard.

§RGain 10 infamy§! While we are no strangers to Syria, the region hasn't been under our control ever since pre-Islamic Iran, with our nation not being able to rule the region ever since the days of Khosrow II of the Sassanids, shortly before the begining of the Muslim conquest of Persia. But now—with our positon as a rising power in the world stage and in the Middle East—we can westle our rivals for control over Syria and the entire Levant—going as far as claiming al-Quds—which would certainly let us be respected not only by Islamic powers, but by Christian ones as well.

§RGain 8 infamy§! While we never ruled over Hedjaz nor does the region have much in the way of economic or strategic importance, its value to us is hard to understate. With our position as the holders of al-Quds, we earned a great deal of respect from the Christian powers and from the Muslim people—to a lesser degree. While al-Quds is also a holy city in Islam, its importance pales in comparison to the Holy Cities of Mecca and Medina—both found in Hedjaz. Thus—pairing it with our position as a great power—if we were to hold both al-Quds and the Holy Cities of Mecca and Medina we would become the uncontested leaders of the Muslim world, even if we are part of the Shiite minority.

The powerful, maritime Sultanate of Muscat-Oman under the capable rule of the BuSaidi dynasty, had managed to occupy much of the coastal lands around the Persian Gulf and the Northwest Indian Ocean, all the way to Zanzibar by the mid 1850s. These included ports, islands and coastal regions of Baluchistan, Strait of Hormuz and Laristan on the Persian side of the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf. These annexations were afforded to Oman during the chaos that ruled Persia in her transitional period between the Zand and the Qajar dynasties, which was followed immediately by the continuous military campaign by Persia defending herself against the imperial Russian and British forces in the north and the east.\n\nDespite losing against the Sultanate of Muscat-Oman in 1846, now that that Muscat lost control over Bandar Abbas, we can once again integrate these ports back into our nation.

\n\nWhile the final version of the Rio-grandense Anthem was only settled for in 1966, the anthem itself was written first right after the capture of Porto Alegre by Rio-grandense forces by a captured military band, with the the official version being written after the end of the war. Composed Joaquim José Medanha, the first version was written by Serafim Joaquim de Alencastre, while the final version was the work of Francisco Pinto da Fontoura.

Ruthenia was always an important part of the Lithuanian state. Even with the Union of Lublin, more than half of the Grand Duchy was composed by Ruthenian voivodeships. Our expansion into Ruthenia began ever before Chirstianization, with the rich cities of Ruthenia granting the resources to fight the repeated agressions of the Teutonic and Livonian Orders. In return, Ruthenian magnates held on to their lands and kept a lot of autonomy under Lithuanian rule, with some Lithuanian nobles even converting to Orthodox Christianity and many of the Grand Duchy's official documents. \n\nOur state has already integrated the White Ruthenians into our nation, but now, with the acquisition of Kiev in the heart of the Rus, we are in a position to tackle the integration of the Ruthenians further south, granting them the same right as the Ruthenians to the north, with a bit of extra autonomy on top of that.

§RGain 8 infamy§! Despite having restored the borders granted by the Napoleon to the Provisional Government Commission of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, that was only the first step of our restoration to the status as an European power. Now that we have annexed Minsk and integrated its people, it is only natural that we push further into uniting the White Ruthenians, while also restoring our pre-partition borders in the process, delving deeper into Russia with it.

Following their occupation of Congress Poland during the Great War, the Act of 5th November was a joint declaration between emperors Wilhelm II of Germany and Franz Joseph of Austria, promising the creation of the Kingdom of Poland out of Congress Poland's territory. The document was born out of a need for Polish blood to fight in the war, with Wilhelm II's Germany even having plans to annex up to 30,000km² of land from the newly-established Kingdom of Poland. Now, with the war over, we are in the position to fulfill our promises to the Poles, letting us further negotiate with our new Polish puppets once the situation stabilizes and the political mood in Poland shifts in our favor.

Lithuanian Jews, nowdays known as Lietvaks, have been an important part of our nations since the days of Vytautas the Great, whom granted privileges to many Lietvaks communities all across the Grand Duchy and ensured a golden age of Judaism in Lithuania, with it leading to the co-existence of both Orthodox Jews and Karaites inside our borders. That is not to say our relation with our Jewish communities was perfect as Lietvaks suffered both from expulsions and conflicts with the nobility. \n\nDespite that, many Jewish communities prospered under our rule, with our capital, Vilnius, being often known by the moniker "Jerusalem of the North", with Lietvaks such as Vilna Gaon and Mendele Mocher Sforim being important figures in the Jewish world. It would prudent to embrace the Lietvaks, guaranteeing their rights and assuring them they are a respected part of our nation.
Granted Equal Rights to the White Ruthenians

§RGain 15 infamy (This will block us from forming the Commonwealth or unite the Baltics!)§! While the Union of Lublin wasn't the first treaty to bring Poland and Lithuania together, with the first being the Union of Krewo, which also established—for the second time—Roman Catholicism as the official religion of Lithuania. Fater the Union of Krewo, many more treaties would deepen the ties between Poland and Lithuania, until the Union of Lublin, which replaced the personal union between both states with a real union, creating the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. 

Despite the Union being agreed on by the Lithuanian representatives, the truth is that it was more of a diktat, with Poland seizing the rich lands of Ruthenia after facing resistance from the Polish representatives, forcing them back into the negotiation table, finally accepting the Union of Lublin under the Polish terms. 

If we were to denounce the Union, we would be able to claim the seized Ruthenian territories once again, at the cost of straining our relationship with the Poles.

§RGain 4 infamy§! Despite allying with Lithuania at one point—during the period in which Mindaugas had converted to Catholicism—Livonia has long been an enemy of Lithuania. Through most of our early history, the Crusaders of Livonia had difficulted our convertion to Christianity, only so they could continue to conquest our land and seize our homes! But, after the Treaty of Vilnius and the Livonian Wars in 1561 Livonia was divided between the Duchies of Livonia and Courland, with Livonia becoming a vassal of the Grand Duke of Lithuania. \n\nNow, with the restoration of our great nation, it is only natural that we renew this old arrangement, claiming Lithuania as an integral part of our nation, together with the Duchy of Courand.
Now that Finland is free, the time has come for $COUNTRY$ to join the motherland!

§RGain 15 infamy§! Being one of the leading causes to the American Revolution, the Quebec Act 1774 was an act of the British Parliament that reformed the governance of the Province of Quebec, guaranteeing the free practive of Catholicism and—more importantly—the expansion of Quebec into parts of Upper Canada and the American states of Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio and Wisconsin. \n\nReaffirming the Quebec Act would for sure anger the Americans, but it would broaden the reach of our ambitions around the Great Lakes region.

§RGain 5 infamy§! The title of King of Galicia-Lodomeria has long been held by the Hungarian kings, with such a title being used by the Habsburg Monarchy to claim the region during the 1st Partition of Poland. But that wasn't the only territory Austria got out of the Partitions of Poland, with New Galicia being awarded to Austria during the 3rd Partition, with the territory being lost to the newly-formed Duchy of Warsaw after the Austrian defeat in the War of the 5th Coalition against Napoleon, with the territory ending up as part of Crogress Poland after the Congress of Vienna. By this point, the Concert of Europe is long gone, allowing us to once again claim these lands as the rightful lords of Galicia-Lodomeria.
Prop up Polish claims to East Prussia

§RGain 7.5 infamy§! With the restoration of the autonomous Kingdom of Poland, we have restored the Polish claims on our neighbors as well. While pressing these claims was another question entirely, it weakened our neighbor significantly, especially the Prussians, with their eastern possessions being divided with the annexation of Gdansk by the Kingdom of Poland. Now with East Prussia cut off from the mainland, we could let Poland lay claim on East Prussia, further solidifying our position in the Baltics.

§RGain 4-8 infamy depending on if you already claimed Greater Iran and Kurdestan§! While we have always claimed Transcaspia as our territory, it was always a hard region to hold on to. Leading us to leave the region alone as we fought to survive the XIXth century. Now—as our nation finished modernizing and taking its place on the world state—we are ready to reaffirm some of our old claims that went unpressed until now, such as the ones in Transcaspia.
With our control over Central Asia established, we need to make sure the borders we drew are enforced! We can't let our control over the region go loose!

With our victory against Afghanistan, we  managed to push the borders of Central Asia further south, seizing the important city of Herat as a result. The region we got from  the Panjdeh Treaty rremains under direct military occupation for now, but preparations are already being made to transfer our gains to our governors in Central Asia, integrating the region into our holdings there. All that is left now is the Tsar's approval for Central Asian troops to move into Northern Afghanistan.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Recently, with our recent overtures to Southern Arabia, through Aden and the Trucial States, the region became of great interest to us. While at first the region provided useful coaling stations to our vessels, with the opening of the construction of the Suez Canal, the Arabian Peninsula suddenly became neighbor to one of the most important waterways in the world, not to mention that, on top the newfound importance of the Red Sea to global trade, the Persian Sea and the Indian Ocean were already home to important trade routes which we already greatly benefited from. 

That said, it is clear that expanding our hold over the Arabian Peninsula is of utmost importance, both to enlarge our current holdings and to prevent any trouble coming from the Peninsula. 

§R(You have to, on top of establishing and expanding both Aden and the Trucial States, sphere/own all cores of Nedj, Hail, Hedjaz, Najran, Oman and Kuwait!)§!

§RGain 10 infamy§! Long departed from the days of its invasions of Persia, Arabia has been reduced to a couple of warring states falling under foreign influences from time to time. Of course, we were quick to take advantage of that fact many times in the past, crossing the Persian Sea and holding land in Eastern Arabia, but these holdings in Arabia were never that permanent, always drifting away from our rule as soon as they had a chance to. 

But now that is about to change. With our recent invasion of Muscat, we have once again a solid holding over Arabia, but that position is disputed currently disputed both by the Arabian tribes and foreign powers. If we were able to hold significant influence over all of Arabia, we could try to leverage the support of the Sharif of Mecca, granting him control over the rest of Arabia, as long as he swears loyalty to us, of course.

§RGain 2.5 infamy§! It has been a long time since our men have been stationed on Bandar-e Lengeh as its rulers. Despíte our rule over the port having long since faded into history, that doesn't mean we didn't try to regain it, but the Sheik of Lengeh and its Qasimi allies have proved to be set on thwarting our attempts at that. But now, after our annexation of neighboring Bandar-e Abbas, annexing Bandar-e Lengeh would consolidate our holdings in Persia. On top of that, with the Qasimi fleet being destroyed and our advances into their Arabian holdings, the Qasimi find themselves in a severely weakened state, which we can't allow the Persians to exploit but would be happy to exploit it ourselves. It is finally time we right the wrongs of history and retake the port from its miserable state.

§RGain 5 infamy (Pay 75,000¤)§! With the consolidation of our holdings in southern Iran, our focus shift into guaranteeing that our interests in the region are secured. While we have consolidated our gains, we quite safe yet, with some suggesting that the only way to secure our holdings being either connecting Gwadar and Bandar-e Abbas by land, or having a bit of a buffer between our ports and the Qajar border. 

Luckily, the Lari and Baluchi tribes present a solution to both propositions at once. Both have been pretty good trade partners to us ever since we established a presence in southern Iran. While it would require a bit of persuasion, but we could try to sway these tribes to join us. The Laris would certainly take quite a bit of "convincing" to joing our cause, but–in contrast—the Baluchis would probably be a bit more open to our overlordship, as long as we keep them safe from the Qajars. 

With both these groups under our thumb, we would be able to not only connect Gwadar and Bandar-e Abbas by land, but also deprive the Qajars from their control over Laristan.

With the Austrian victory in the Bruderkrieg, Germany's only counterweight to Austrian influence was officially defeated, with Prussia being stripped of the its great power status. While the German states were effectively puppets of both Austria and Prussia, with the Prussian defeat, the Austrian influence over the German states now lies unopposed, with Austrian having reformed the Federal Convention in Frankfurt, allowing them to use it to control the German states through this new German Confederation and declare themselves Emperors of Germany. \n\nWhile the German states still hold varying degrees of autonomy, the Federal Convention in Frankfurt still holds the authority to impose legislation over all members of the Confederation, being able to overrule local laws and reserving the right to legislate about specific matters, with the members of the Confederation having to pay taxes to the Federal Convention in Frankfurt for the maintainance of the Federal City of Frankfurt, the Federal Army and the Reichsflotte. The Federal Convetion was used to curtail our liberty and make us answer to the Austrian Emperor, on top of being subject to further diktats from Vienna.

Our victory in the Bruderkrieg gave us total hegemony over Germany. With Prussia knocked out of their great power status, nobody can oppose us in Germany anymore. Because of that, we were free to reform the German Confederation to not only claim the title of Emperor of Germany but to use the Federal Convention in Frankfurt to control the other German states as well—confirming their status as our puppets. \n\nWhile the German states still hold varying degrees of autonomy, the Federal Convention in Frankfurt still holds the authority to impose legislation over all members of the Confederation, being able to overrule local laws and reserving the right to legislate about specific matters, with the members of the Confederation having to pay taxes to the Federal Convention in Frankfurt for the maintainance of the Federal City of Frankfurt, the Federal Army and the Reichsflotte, but we are excluded for such taxes, of course.

When Prussia was defeated, the Hohenzollerns were expelled from their holdings in Brandenburg, being forced to live in exile in Königsberg. Brandenburg became an "independent" state inside of the German Confederation under the tutelage of Austria, of course. 

We can't say that such transition came easy however. We can't deny that some of our government wasn't quite sold on the idea of Austrian Hegemony over Germany, and it seems that Vienna caught on to that. 

A while ago, the Austrian monarch—now Emperor of Germany—came into the Federal Convention revealing the existence of a plot inside of our government seeking to return to Hohenzollern rule. While we can't be sure if such plot was real or not, it lead the Federal Convention to call for an joint Austro-Saxon occupation of our state, leading us to be firmly under the Austrian thumb from now own.
The Seat of the German Federal Convention

Second only to Vienna (and Berlin before Prussia's defeat), Frankfurt is one of the most important cities in Germany. As a center of German culture, Frankfurt was the seat of the Federal Convention and the capital of the German Confederation ever since the Congress of Vienna. That didn't change with the Austrian victory in the Bruderkrieg—on the contrary—Frankfurt became pivotal to Austria's plans to control the German Confederation. \n\nAustria has, in practice, reformed the German Confederation, effectively turning the Federal Convention into its puppet and being able to use it to control the other German states. Now, as the Federal City of Frankfurt, we are the formal capital of the new and reformed German Confederation, complicit in Vienna's diktats to the German world, having crowned the Austrian Emperor as the Emperor of Germany in exchange for collecting taxes on our fellow German states.

While Riveira appointed Oribe as his successor, he remained in charge of the armed forces of Uruguay for a while. But, as one of the 33 Orientals, Oribe loyalty to Riveira is fragile at best, with some pointing out that both men have been rivals ever since the days of Artigas. With Oribe's ascension to power, friction between the two man began to appear, with Oribe soon deciding to take away Riveira's position at the command of the Uruguayan Army and pardon Lavalleja for his attempts against Riveira's life and government.

For a long time, two projects of country divided Argentina. Unitarianists or Unitarians were the proponents of the concept of a Unitary state (centralized government) in Buenos Aires and they were led by  Juan Lavalle. They were opposed to the Argentine Federalists, who wanted a federation of independent provinces, led by Juan Manuel de Rosas. The Unitarians, sympathetic to our government, fled Argentina in exile after being defeated in 1831. Rosas, the so called Restorer of the Laws, controlled the Argentine Confederation for too long under his despotic rule. Now, our friends in Uruguay defeated the Blancos and promise to support us if we were to fight the Federalists to end Rosas despotic ruler.

§RVarela will be assassinated in march 1848, so be sure to take this decision before that!§! The Unitarians during the Big War counted not only with the support of Uruguay but also limited Anglo-French support. While both nations couldn't wage direct war with Rosas without allies to the ground, we could send Florencio Varela to negotiate with France and Britain for support, with the permission to take desperate measures if needed.

On May 1st, 1851, General and Governor Justo José de Urquiza, unsatisfied with the lack of the return of the trade-primacy of Buenos Aires after the end of the Anglo-French Blockade and Rosas lack of a proper constitution for the Argentine Confederation decreed the Urquiza's Statement, on which he formally accepted Rosas resignation—which he applied for every year, knowing his resignation as foreign relations minister would be rejected—declaring the effective independence of the Province of Entre Rios until a proper General Assembly for the writing of a constitution was called. \n\nUrquiza's Statement was supported by his political pupil Benjamín Virasoro—Governor of Corrientes—which until now was considered one of Rosas' partisans. Rosas, in the other hand, naturally rejected the statement.

§RGain 5 infamy§! Between foreign and personal interests, to some degree, Entre Rios independence from the Argentine Confederation was founded on bases of the wish to uphold the ideals of Federalism. To reinforce our place as the bastion of "True Federalism", we could—to some degree—claim to be the true successor to the League of the Free Peoples, the state that—under José Gervasio Artigas—gave birth to the Federalist movement in Argentina. Doing so would put us at odds with our old allies, which now occupy territory which was once part of the League and would also rekindle our hostilities with Buenos Aires, which not only may still claim to be successors to the League, but also hold the Province of Córdoba, which was also part of the League to some degree.
Claim the Mantle of the League of the Free Peoples

§RGain 5 infamy§! With the birth of the Uruguayan Federation and the integration of the Gauchos from Rio Grande do Sul, the old ties between Uruguay and the local population have been rekindled. Despite the differences between us and the local population, we faced a lot of sympathetic sentiment in the region, with some like-minded even offering to pull some strings to find support across the northern border, in Santa Catarina, to try and give us a chance to claim the region. Santa Catarina was once occupied by the Rio-grandense Republic during the Ragamuffin War, with the Juliana Republic being established. With support from the Farrapos in Rio Grande do Sul, we could claim the region and shorten our border with Brazil significantly.

§RGain 10 infamy§! During the Platine Wars of Independence, Paraguay's fate stood on the edge of a knife. At the start, during the First Junta of Buenos Aires, Manuel Belgrano tried to invade Paraguay to liberate it from Royalist forces. Not only Belgrano in that task but Artigas also tried to incorporate Paraguay in the League of the Free Peoples, an prospect that also found no success. With both failed attempts on the conquest of Paraguay by Platine forces, the country's independence was secured. But now—as we carry the mantle of the League of the Free Peoples—Paraguay stands as the only country—besides us—between Argentina and Brazil. Thus, conquering it would not only avenge Artigas' attempt, but also become a stronger buffer between the two giants that border us.

Very little progress has been made in the past few thousand years on that greatest of all building projects initiated by our proud ancestors. With Mesopotamia's recent ascent to power and standing in the world, there is some talk... though all talk has been strangely hard to understand lately... of starting the project back up again! With modern technology, who knows what wonders could be accomplished?
French: Au cours des derniers millénaires, très peu de progrès ont été faits sur le plus grand projet de construction initié par nos illustres ancêtres. Avec la montée en puissance récente et la nouvelle place dans le concert des nation de l'Iraq, on parle - même si récemment, le discourt s'est fait incompréhensible - de relancer le projet ! Avec la technologie moderne, qui sait quelles merveilles pourraient être accomplies ?
German: Im Laufe der letzten Jahrtausende wurden beim größten aller Bauprojekte, begonnen von unseren stolzen Vorfahren, kaum noch Fortschritte erzielt. Durch den kürzlichen Aufstieg des Iraks zu Macht und Ansehen in der Welt gibt es Gespräche ... die in letzter Zeit merkwürdigerweise nur schwer zu verstehen waren ... das Projekt wieder aufzunehmen! Welche Wunder wohl durch den Einsatz moderner Technologie möglich wären?
Spanish: En los últimos milenios apenas se han hecho progresos en el mayor de los proyectos de construcción iniciado por nuestros orgullosos antepasados. ¡Con el reciente ascenso de Irak en el concierto de las naciones, cada vez más voces (aunque cada vez más confusas, también es cierto) hablan de reiniciar el proyecto! Con la tecnología moderna, ¿quién sabe qué maravillas se podrían alcanzar?

English: When Rivera—with help from his Anglo-French backers—deposed Oribe, Rosas was the man which not only hosted Oribe in exile, but also went to war to restore Oribe to the Uruguayan presidency. Now, as Oribe sits at the head of the Uruguayan politics once again, Rosas is facing problems back home, with the governor of Entre Rios—José Justo de Urquiza—revolting against him. It is about time we return the favor and help Rosas against this insurgency.

The traitor José Justo de Urquiza once commissioned journalist and historian Pedro de Angelis a constitution. While Urquiza was defeated by our great leader Rosas, the constitutional project went ahead, with the finished 135-long constitution being published in Angelis' journal in Buenos Aires. Rosas—at first—personally wasn't very keen on Angelis and his work, but with time our great leader approached Angelis personally to publish some intellectual projects of his government, creating a bridge between the two men. \n\nWith Rosismo evolving and Rosas' health starting to fade, it may be for the best that—instead of relying on Rosas' son to carry his regime on—we commission Angelis' constitution to be sanctioned as the official constitution of the Argentine Confederation.

§RGain 10 infamy§! "Relations with the Province of Paraguay, which have been severed for many years, will be definitively restored by the first Legislative Congress that meets after the present Constitution is sworn in." — These are the exact words in Angelis' Constitution. While vague, Angelis confessed—at a later date—to including it as a path to reintegrate Paraguay into the Confederation. Paraguay has long been a great reason of shame and a thorn in our side, with its dictator—Carlos Antonio López—having supported both the Unitarians in Corrientes and the traitors under Urquiza. But—following Angelis draft—we have established negotiations with Asunción which have yet to be fruitful. Maybe it is about time we cut off our relations with Paraguay and end their independence once and for all.

Our old disputes with the Federalist Party led to our secession from the old Argentine Confederation. With the fall of the Federalist government, the Unitarians took over Argentina, destroying the old confederation and declared the creation of the Argentinian Republic, which closely alligns with our ideals. Perhaps now it's time we finally rejoin Buenos Aires...
The Rights of the First Peoples

While we can't say the Federalist Party is ideologically aligned with the idea of indigenous rights, our ideology and political structure always favored great cooperation with the local indigenous peoples. Artigas was the first to do so, with his policies and networks reaching the indigenous peoples. Besides that, as the Federalist model favored local power, Federalist caudillos were quick to use the local natives to their advantage, not to mention that nods to the native population weren't an exclusive Federalist phenomenon, with the declaration of independence by the Congress of Tucumán being published in Spanish, Quechua and Aimara.

Our great leader holds total authority over the society and seeks to control all aspects of public and private life wherever possible, seeing himself as a "benevolent dictator" and a father to our people. He reaches so far as to dictate how people dress and carry themselves, plastering the symbols of the regime all over the country. In contrast, anyone opposed to his absolute authority is forced into hiding, or faces punishment in prison or even is made an example by our leader's agents. The entire population is, willingly or unwillingly, conscripted to serve our leader's priorities and subject to his whims.

With the revolt in Buenos Aires following Rosas being overthrown, we have been left in a precarious position. We have lost the country's most important port and our coffers are running drier from the loss of its revenue, hindering our ability to muster large armies for prolonged periods of time.

Until now, Paraná has been the Federal capital of the Argentine Confederation ever since Rosas was deposed and Buenos Aires broke away from us. But now, with the matter of Buenos Aires dealt with, it is finally time we decide on a definitive capital for the Argentine Confederation, lest the savages in Buenos Aires find a way to let their city be our capital once again.

Our country is currently ruled by a governmental and intellectual elite of positivist oligarchs that are bent on staying on power by any means necessary—while keeping the guise of a democratic government, of course.

§RGain 2.5-5 infamy, depending on if you or your puppet own Cusco!§! Despite the shifting economic and political developments since independence, South Peru stills remains connected to Bolivia in one way or another. This connection has long been the a point of contention between Peru and Bolivia, even leading to Santa Cruz's Peru-Bolivian Confederation at one point, but before that, the connection between South Peru and Bolivia—in face of the independence war and concerns over Lima's stability—pushed one of our heroes, San Martín, into considering the possibility of an autonomous South Peruvian protectorate, under Platine—or Chilean—supervision. While the days of our independence war are long over, with our growing dominance over South Andean affair, we could try to use such plans to our advantage and detach South Peru from Lima, strengthening its connections to old Bolivia, allowing us to expand our great state and placate the people of Alto Peru.

Despite his old age, the return of San Martín was met with joy by most of the Argentine Confederation. The hero has since returned to military service and even if his role is limited due to his advancing age, his mere presence is enough to raise our morale and increase our prestige in the region!

§RGain 5 infamy§! Argentina has many heros, but they all pale in comparison to San Martín. The legacy of the Father of the Fatherland is felt even beyond our borders, with our hero even being a revered figure in Chile and Peru, besides O'Higgins and Bolívar respectively. \n\nNow that we became a stable great power in the Southern Cone, it is only natural we consider how his legacy could be used to influence the other nations on which he is celebrated.
The Sister Republic Across the Andes

§RGain 7.5 infamy§! With the failure of the Army of the North, San Martín—correctly—determined that securing Chilean independence would be pivotal to secure Platine independence in the face of the failures in Alto Peru. His plans would come to fruition with the Army of the Andes and the Chilean Declaration of Independence following the Battle of Maipú. While our relations were friendly—with our armies fighting together against the Peru-Bolivian Confederation—disputes would slowly surface over our borders in Patagonia the Andes, leading to a falling out between our two nations. Our newly announced ambitions served only to grow the rift between our nations further, leaving us no choice but to turn their worse fears into reality and leave clear our intention to force them into our beautiful union.

§RGain 5-15 infamy§! When San Martín liberated Peru, he worried that the Liman elites would impose their will on the rest of the country and, whether this happened or not, we used it to justify our take over of South Peru and—now that South Peru has been dealt with—our next objetive lies in completely dominating Lima and the rest of Peru, with the hopes of preparing it for a future union between our nations.

To Unitarism, the Interior is a hassle—a savage land of uncivilized natives, unruly gauchos and despotic caudillos. Our control over the Interior is weak, with our appointed governors west of Córdoba having a hard time not being toppled by local rivals and Federalist revolts. While we can keep supressing the Interior, it is clear that having to do so only depletes our resources and leaves us open to being toppled by the Federalists once again. \n\nIf we are to finally subdue the Savage Interior, we need to not only modernize our administration of the territory, but also reform our military structure so charismatic tyrants can't threaten our governors with the help of militant gauchos anymore.

With our recent conquest of Alto Peru, we are met with a challenge. Alto Peru—nowdays known as Bolivia—was always meant to be part of Argentina, but due to the Army of the North's failture to liberate the region, the region would end up becoming its own nation which—much to our dismay—ended up enacting a policy of trying to distance itself from us. While we now control Alto Peru for the first time since our independence, the damage is already done, as we now need to invest in the the local population so that they see that we are kin and meant to fight side-by-side as brothers for $COUNTRY$!

Ever since the first days of our independence, many had a vision of Alto Peru—also known as Bolivia—being part of our nation. Sadly, now this vision has come into fruition, it became clear the the people of Alto Peru hardly have accepted the fact that they are now a part of our nation. Luckily—with some nice gestures showing our commitment to them—we can reintegrate them and teach their place in our great nation.

§RGain 24.99 infamy§! In 1816, in the wake of Argentinian Independence, Manuel Belgrano proposed that not only La Plata, Chile and Peru should unite under single nation, but also that—to gather recognition from the European powers—such a nation should crown a monarch, an Inca monarch to be more precise. Now that we went through with such plans to crown an Inca King, it is about time that we seize our position as a rising power to declare the need to realize the 1816 Inca Plan and unite most of Hispanic South America under our great monarchy!
Force Isfandiyar Khan to publish the Young Khivans Manifesto

With the recent wave of revolts and revolutionary movements across Central Asia and especially Khiva, the Young Khivans have the perfect opportunity to force Isfandiyar Khan into signing a manifesto establishing a legislative Majlis and put prominent Young Khivan Bobohun Salimov as its chairman. Despite the Khan being bound to accept, as a conservative we know that he won't be happy with the arrangement and will look for a way of undermining the Young Khivans to recover his power.

§RGain 2.5 infamy§! With the war against Brazil, a certain sense of brotherhood was created between the Unitarian Party and the Colorado Party. Despite both parties having their differences, after the war such differences seem small in comparison to their shared enemies. Not only that, but many Colorados ended up becoming more "Unitarian-minded" during the war. Maybe it would be a good idea to use our connections in the Colorado Party to put forward the union between Uruguay and Argentina. That would mean, of course, betraying Rivera and his republic, but that would be a small price to pay for Platinean Unity...

§RGain 4 infamy§! With our rule over Herat consolidated and Britain out of the way for now, we are finally ready to shift our attention towards our next objective: The Emirate of Kandahar. The rulers of Kandahar, while appearing subservient to the Peacock Throne, having recently supported us in sieging Herat in exchange for the border province of Farah and Sabzevar, enjoys far too much autonomy and free movement to be considered a proper subject of Iran. \nKandahar is not simply a dependency of Iran, but an integral part of our domain and it is time to establish this fact. Let us send a full expedition to Kandahar and demand the total submission of the Emir.

§RGain 2.5 infamy§! Our claim over the Bahrain Archipelago has always been complicated. With its population being mostly of Shiite-Iranian origin, we have traditionally ruled the area in an indirect manner, through the al-Mazkur Sheikhs of Bushehr. While we still hold a traditional claim to these islands, they haven't been under direct Iranian control since the Zand Dynasty, with Manamah currently ruled by the Sunni Banu Utub dynasty of Nejddi origin who have refused to reconize any kind of rule from Tehran, going as far as getting protection from the British to keep themselves free from our dominion. \n\nWhile we previously managed to strike an agreement with the British for the reincorporation of Bahrain into our state, the vile Europeans went back on their word, refusing to return Bahrain to us. It is about time we reaffirm our claims to Bahrain, with no regard to what the British or any other foreign power thinks about it!
Kandahar's autonomy has served us well. But, with the modernization of our state, it is about time we strip him of some of his rights to better control the region.

§RGain 1 infamy§! Less than 300km from Herat lies the city of Maymana, an important center of commerce in the region and our gateway to Turkestan. The city—mostly inhabited by Uzbeks these days—sits at the middle of the Chahar Vilayets, a region inhabited by 4 khanates, Sar-i Pul, Sheberghan, Andkhui and—the most powerful and influential of them all—Maymana. Despite that, the Chahar Vilayets as a whole were far from stable, with the 4 khanates finding themselves at war with each other from time to time, not to mention when foreign powers such as Herat and Kabul having long coveted the region and especially Maymana—reconizing its importance in the region and the potential to control the rest of the khanates through the city. Now that Herat is firmly annexed into our nation, it is about time we bring order to the Chahar Vilayets by invading Maymana, securing our borders in the region and assuring our oversight over the region and its remaining khans!

The Turkmen and Uzbek Tribes have long been raiding our our northern territory, pillaging and taking some of our people captive to be sold as slaves. Many of these tribes act on the interests of the Khan of Khiva and the Emir of Bukhara, both of which profit greatly of the influx of slaves and riches captured by these raids. To deal with those troublesome tribals, we will have to first deal with Khiva and Bukhara—to leave the Turkmen and Uzbek tribes helpless against our advances and maybe even being able to end the trading of Iranian slaves in Khiva.

With we being successful in putting an end to the raids that plagued our northern border, the Turkmen tribes that once relied on these raids have grown weak. If we were to better develop our administration, we could pacify one and for all those weakened tribes before our neighbors to the north can take advantage of them in our place.

§RGain 5 infamy§! The region around Balkh—also known as Little Turkestan—has long been a contested between Iranian and Central Asian powers, with control over it shifting constantly back in the days of the Safavid Dynasty. The region nowdays is mostly contested between the Emirs of Bukhara and Kabul, with both having recently gained a stronger foothold in the region with local khans pledging allegiance to them as a to guarantee some sort of protection against us. While some of our advisors aren't sure about expanding eastwards, the truth is not doing so would be dooming the region to being dominated by either Kabul or Bukhara. Taking over the region—currently inhabited by Uzbeks—would not only deprive our rivals of useful land, but also isolate them from one another so we can take them out one at a time. \n\n§RYou need at least 75% civilization progress, the tooltip lies.§W
Take Control of the Amu Darya

§RGain 7.5 infamy§! With our successful campaigns in Balkh and Kunduz, fraying the local patchwork Warlords and Khans, we now hold control over the upper Amu Darya, a great river serving as the lifeblood of Central Asia's great settlements, including the city of Khiva. While it seems obvious to move down-stream to assert our control over the river's entire length, exerting control over the lands past the right bank of the river would prove too much for our nation's administration. Instead, we could subjugate the Emirate of Bukhara as a representative of the Shah's dominion over Transoxiana, a once mighty polity with a long and storied history of ruling the region that would help us assert control over the great Silk Road cities of Shahrisabz, Qarshi, Samarkand and Bukhara itself. 

We have already butted heads with Bukhara once already our success there assures us that they will be no match to our great state!

With our administration modernized and control over Transoxiana and the Emirate of Bukhara pacified, it is about time we finally cross the Amu Darya and end Bukhara's autonomy before they become a problem for us, opening way for us to further influence Central Asia. \n\nAlso, we will take the opportunity to finally put an end to the pitiful khanate ruled by the Karakalpaks across the river from Khiva!

With our advances into Mesopotamia and Kurdistan we have promptly usurped the Ottoman position as the overlords Mesopotamia and Eastern Anatolia, leading to our annexation of cities such as Baghdad, Mosul and Erzurum. Now, having defeated the Turks once again, we are in a position to pressure the Turks into signing a treaty to ratify the current border as permanent, to put and end to the hostilities between our nations. \n\nOf course, that would imply that we don't want to expand further into ther holdings, but that is a small price to pay for not having the risk of them striking us at our moment of weakness.

§RGain 5 infamy§!Now that we have established our dominion over Transoxiana, it is hard to say that our ambitions in the region are satisfied. Instead, we have to note that, while we managed to secure our hold over Bukhara and Samarkand, those cities are hard to defend, considering how far they are from our holdings in Iran. Counterintuitively, the way to solve this would be to push further into Central Asia, dominating the Sart-dominated Urban centers of Tashkent and Kokand, claiming a line from the Ferghana Valley to the Syr Darya.
Call Iran into the Crimean War

§RGain 5 infamy§! As the Crimean War rages on, it became clear that the powers of Europe are plotting against our position in the Concert of Europe! Starved out of our conventional allies in Europe, it becomes clear that—to tip the war in our favor—we need to resort to one of our unusual pawns—the Qajars of Iran! \n\nWe would offer the Qajars parts of Kurdistan and—in exchange—they would join our war against the Turks, opening a new front, distracting the Ottoman and French armies—letting our armies siege Constantinople in no time!

§RGain 5 infamy§!We have held a great deal of influence in Iraq ever since the Turkish defeat in the Crimean War, which led to the region being effectively independent ever since. Now, with our growing role in the region and foreign interest in Mesopotamia increasing, it is clear that—if we are to keep our investments in the region—we need to hold a tighter grip over Mesopotamia. The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ resident in Baghdad has spend the last few months negotiating with the Prince of Iraq for the principality to accept a protectorate status under our empire—to no avail. We are left no choice but to coup the Iraqi prince and ensure that Baghdad will be ruled by someone more willing to cooperate with us...

§RGain 8 infamy§!Now that we have decisively beaten the Ottomans we are free to enforce our claims in the region and force the Turks into the negotiating table, ensuring the victory of our Russian allies!
